Moreover, the Supreme Court has held that "not all disparate treatment claims require proof of discriminatory motive; some may be proved through a showing of disparate impact." (See Griggs v. Duke Power Co., 401 U.S. 424, 431 (1971)).

Furthermore, the Seventh Circuit has held that "statistics alone are not sufficient to establish a prima facie case of disparate treatment under Title VII." (See Smith v. City of Chicago, 769 F.3d 874, 880 (7th Cir. 2014)). In Wrenfield, the Eighth Circuit's decision was actually based on the plaintiff's failure to provide evidence of a similarly situated comparator, rather than any showing of statistical disparities or supervisor remarks about cultural "fit." (See Wrenfield v. Ozark Regional Medical Center, 738 F.3d 512, 517 (8th Cir. 2014)).

Ozark Regional Medical Center does not support the claim that inconsistent application of subjective performance evaluations can be evidence of pretext in a Title VII disparate treatment claim.
